diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Under Assumption~\ref{assu:gaussian_tail_function_space}, the Föllmer velocity field
$v(t,\cdot)$ associated with transporting $\rho=\mathcal N(0,C)$ to $\pi(\cdot\mid y_{\mathrm{obs}})$
is globally Lipschitz and satisfies
\[
\mathrm{Lip}\big(v(t,\cdot)\big)\le L_0\,t,\quad \forall\,t\in[0,1],
\]

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma/Theorem C.3 claims that the averaged velocity field satisfies Lip(w(·; r, t)) <= (t - r)^{-1} int_r^t Lip(v(tau, ·)) dtau <= L_0 (t + r)/2 without proof. This estimate is mathematically false for the flow-averaged velocity w_{r,t} = (t - r)^{-1} int_r^t v(z_tau, tau) dtau because it ignores the spatial sensitivity of the trajectories z_tau: the derivative D_z w(z; r, t) contains the flow Jacobian D_z z_tau, which by Grönwall's inequality grows exponentially with the Lipschitz constant of v. For instance, in 1D with dz/dt = -a z (a > 0), Lip(v) = a, but the backward flow satisfies z_tau = z e^{a(t - tau)}, giving Lip(w(·; r, t)) = (e^{a(t - r)} - 1)/(t - r) > a = (t - r)^{-1} int_r^t Lip(v) dtau. In addition, Theorem C.3 assumes Theorem C.2, which bounds the Föllmer velocity of a Schrödinger bridge/process, whereas the paper's Mean Flows model uses linear-path flow matching, whose marginal velocity field is fundamentally distinct from the Föllmer drift.

failure_location.quote:
Assume Theorem~\ref{thm:dimfree_lip_velocity}. Then average velocity $w(\cdot;r,t)$ for $0\le r\le t\le 1$ is globally Lipschitz and
\[
\mathrm{Lip}\big(w(\cdot;r,t)\big)
\le \frac{1}{t-r}\int_r^t \mathrm{Lip}\big(v(\tau,\cdot)\big)\,d\tau
\le L_0\,\frac{t+r}{2}.
\]
In particular, $\mathrm{Lip}\big(w(\cdot;0,1)\big)\le L_0/2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish the regularity of the linear-path Mean Flows velocity field under the prior-aligned geometry and bound the Lipschitz constant of the resulting flow map using flow sensitivity estimates (which produce an exponential Grönwall factor rather than an additive linear bound).
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical guarantees establishing that the averaged velocity field w and the one-step transport map T(·; y_obs) are globally Lipschitz with dimension-free bounds Lip(T) <= 1 + L_0/2 (Theorem 3.1, Theorem C.3, Corollary C.4) are unproven and invalid.
issues.title: Invalid Lipschitz bound for averaged velocity and one-step transport
issues.why_classification: Establishing the Lipschitz regularity of the one-step transport map is the central theoretical result advertised for the proposed prior-aligned method. Correcting the invalid trajectory bound requires fundamentally changing the guarantee to exponential Grönwall-type bounds, and proving regularity for the conditional expectation velocity field of Mean Flows in function space requires entirely new proof architecture not supported by the source.
